analyst_view.overall: Another relegation six-pointer: Paderborn (15th, 10 points) host Schalke (16th, 7 points), two promoted sides who both struggle to score. Paderborn lost 4-0 at Leverkusen last time out under Ralf Kettemann; Schalke drew 0-0 with Stuttgart and are without a win in seven league games, but Miron Muslic's job is described as safe. Schalke have a long injury list this autumn (Timo Becker, Gosens, Wöber, Gantenbein among those reported out in recent weeks) and Bryan Lasme missed the start of this week with a thigh problem; none of this is in the numbers' missing list, but most of those players were already absent in the recent games the numbers are built on. No referee is named yet. I only add a few cards for the stakes.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.5 goals, already low because Schalke have scored only 2 in six and Paderborn rarely score either. Lasme's doubt and Schalke's injuries fit that picture rather than change it, so I stay at 1.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners and already trim a little for both teams' recent form. Both sides will push in a must-win game, but nothing in the news changes their style, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.1 cards, low because both teams have been booked rarely lately (Paderborn 6 in six, already counted). A 15th-versus-16th game with points this tight is usually more physical than these teams' average, which the numbers don't count, so I add 5%, to about 2.2; no referee is named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, with both teams' recent shot counts already in. Paderborn started with a lone striker at Leverkusen, but at home they should be more open, so I stay at 28.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Schalke's attack has been blunt and Lasme may miss out, but that is already part of their recent record, so I stay at 8.6.
